answer: Epoch-Linked Behavioural Continuity. Each identity's actions across epochs must remain consistent in timing and interaction patterns; an agent acts as a bridge between epochs only if its prior record predicts its next actions within tolerance. Every identity is a vertex in a per-epoch behaviour graph, and an identity whose graph position shifts abruptly is flagged. Attacker cost: sustaining many identities through this check requires continuously generating coherent histories, roughly matching one full epoch of genuine activity per identity, so the fable of cheap mass identities collapses.
